title: nolabs-ai/claude default configuration allows communication with host processes (e.g. Docker) and therefore a potential sandbox escape
body:
With the default configuration of the nolabs-ai/claude pack, Claude can communicate with processes on the host via Unix sockets. If a Docker daemon is running and the logged-in user is in the docker group, Claude can escape the nono sandbox and gain root access to the host by starting a new Docker container with a volume mount.

nono is advertised as a secure sandbox environment. Users pick nono to keep an agent away from the host. Not running daemons on the host isn't a realistic option: developer machines typically run Docker, databases, ssh-agent, D-Bus and similar services. That's precisely the environment an agent sandbox has to cope with.

The setting that prevents this, `af_unix_mediation`, should therefore be turned on by default. The documentation should explicitly warn against turning it off. The setting is mentioned on the [Landlock internals page](https://nono.sh/docs/cli/internals/landlock#pathname-unix-socket-mediation): "For compatibility, this mediation is off by default." I'm not sure what "compatibility" refers to here. Blocking communication with host processes is exactly what a sandbox is for. Sockets the agent actually needs can be granted explicitly.

Other profiles or operating systems might be affected too. I haven't checked or tested them.

This topic was first discussed in a private security advisory, [GHSA-x82j-3724-gch8](https://github.com/nolabs-ai/nono/security/advisories/GHSA-x82j-3724-gch8). As suggested by the maintainers, I'm now opening this public issue.

## Workaround

A profile that extends the pack and enables mediation blocks the Docker socket:

```
{
  "extends": "nolabs-ai/claude",
  "meta": { "name": "claude-unix" },
  "linux": { "af_unix_mediation": "pathname" }
}
```

Save it as e.g. `~/.config/nono/profiles/claude-unix.json` and run nono with `--profile ~/.config/nono/profiles/claude-unix.json`. With it, docker run inside the sandbox fails with permission denied while trying to connect to the docker API at `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`.

## Environment

nono 0.80.0, Linux 6.1 (Debian), Landlock V2
